entries.title: Mana Well
entries.body:
# Mana Well

## Overview
Before a Spellblade can master arcane combat, they must first master the vessel that contains their power. Through relentless training, meditation, and repeated exposure to mana, the Spellblade learns to expand the natural limits of their internal mana reserves.

This expansion creates the foundation of what Spellblades call a Mana Well—a deep reservoir of magical energy that fuels both their martial techniques and arcane abilities. While many novice practitioners focus on increasing their offensive power, experienced Spellblades understand that sustained combat is won by those who can continue fighting long after others have exhausted their resources.

At Rank 1, the Mana Well begins to take shape. The increase is immediately noticeable, allowing the Spellblade to cast additional abilities, maintain magical techniques for longer periods, and remain effective during extended encounters.

Though only the beginning of the talent's growth, many masters consider Mana Well one of the most important foundations of the entire Spellblade path. A deeper well creates opportunities, endurance, and flexibility that cannot be replicated through skill alone.

## Rank 1
### Description

Before a Spellblade can master arcane combat, they must first master the vessel that contains their power. Through relentless training, meditation, and repeated exposure to mana, the Spellblade learns to expand the natural limits of their internal mana reserves.

This expansion creates the foundation of what Spellblades call a Mana Well—a deep reservoir of magical energy that fuels both their martial techniques and arcane abilities. While many novice practitioners focus on increasing their offensive power, experienced Spellblades understand that sustained combat is won by those who can continue fighting long after others have exhausted their resources.

At Rank 1, the Mana Well begins to take shape. The increase is immediately noticeable, allowing the Spellblade to cast additional abilities, maintain magical techniques for longer periods, and remain effective during extended encounters.

Though only the beginning of the talent's growth, many masters consider Mana Well one of the most important foundations of the entire Spellblade path. A deeper well creates opportunities, endurance, and flexibility that cannot be replicated through skill alone.

### Effects

- Increase your **Maximum Mana by ×3**.
- This multiplier is applied to your **Base Maximum Mana**.
- The increase is permanent while this talent is learned.
- The additional mana becomes immediately available upon learning the talent.

#### Formula

Maximum Mana = Base Mana × 3

### Lore

Among Spellblades, the cultivation of a Mana Well is considered the first true milestone on the path toward mastery. While a sword may be sharpened and spells may be memorised, neither can compensate for a lack of magical endurance.

The oldest Spellblade academies teach that mana is like water carried into a vast desert. Every technique draws from the same reserve, and once that reserve is exhausted, even the greatest warrior becomes vulnerable.

Many legendary Spellblades became famous not because they possessed the most destructive abilities, but because they could continue fighting long after their opponents had depleted their strength. Their Mana Wells sustained them through battles that would have broken lesser combatants.

For this reason, instructors often insist that apprentices strengthen their reserves before pursuing more advanced techniques. A strong foundation supports every future achievement.

> "Power is meaningless when the well runs dry."
>
> — Master Valen Arcturus, Seventh Blade of the Azure Order

## Rank 2
### Description

As the Spellblade's mastery grows, so too does the depth of their Mana Well. What was once a modest reservoir begins to expand into a substantial source of arcane power, capable of sustaining increasingly demanding techniques.

The cultivation of a Mana Well is not simply a matter of storing more mana. The Spellblade learns to strengthen the pathways through which mana flows, reinforcing their body and soul so they can safely contain greater quantities of magical energy. Without this growth, advanced techniques would place unbearable strain upon the practitioner.

At Rank 2, the Spellblade experiences a significant increase in their available reserves. Battles that once required careful conservation of mana become easier to manage, allowing the Spellblade to maintain pressure and continue casting throughout longer encounters.

Many instructors consider this the point where an apprentice begins to transition into a true Spellblade. Their reserves become large enough to support both martial combat and arcane techniques without constantly risking exhaustion.

### Effects
- Increase your **Maximum Mana by ×6**.
- This multiplier is applied to your **Base Maximum Mana**.
- The additional mana becomes immediately available upon learning the talent.

#### Formula

Maximum Mana = Base Mana × 6

### Lore

Veteran Spellblades often describe Rank 2 as the point where the Mana Well becomes impossible to ignore. The increase in magical endurance is substantial enough that even inexperienced practitioners immediately notice the difference.

The process is neither comfortable nor quick. Expanding one's Mana Well requires months of disciplined training, repeated mana circulation exercises, and careful refinement of the soul's connection to arcane energy. Many students abandon the process due to its difficulty.

Those who persevere are rewarded with reserves that can sustain far more demanding techniques. This increase allows them to remain active during prolonged battles, maintaining the balance between swordsmanship and spellcraft that defines the Spellblade path.

The ancient records of the Azure Orders speak of Mana Wells as living reservoirs. The deeper they become, the more power they can hold, and the greater the possibilities available to the one who wields them.

> "The first well grants endurance. The second grants freedom."
>
> — Grand Spellblade Aethon Vale, Master of the Sapphire Hall

## Rank 3
### Description

The Mana Well has grown beyond a simple reservoir and now resembles a vast internal lake of arcane power. The Spellblade's body and soul have adapted to contain quantities of mana that would overwhelm most practitioners, allowing them to wield magic with far greater freedom.

At this stage, mana conservation becomes less about necessity and more about efficiency. The Spellblade can maintain prolonged combat techniques, sustain enchantments for longer periods, and continue casting long after others would be forced to retreat and recover.

The cultivation of such a Mana Well requires extraordinary discipline. Every increase places additional strain upon the pathways that carry mana throughout the body. Those who fail to strengthen themselves alongside their reserves risk injury, magical exhaustion, or complete mana collapse.

For many Spellblades, Rank 3 marks the point where they truly begin to feel the potential of their path. Their magical endurance becomes a defining advantage, allowing them to fight longer, cast more frequently, and adapt to changing battlefield conditions without fear of immediate depletion.

### Effects

- Increase your **Maximum Mana by ×9**.
- This multiplier is applied to your **Base Maximum Mana**.
- The additional mana becomes immediately available upon learning the talent.

#### Formula

Maximum Mana = Base Mana × 9

### Lore

Ancient Spellblade texts often describe Rank 3 as the threshold between the ordinary and the exceptional. While many warriors learn to wield magic and many mages learn to fight, few possess the reserves necessary to excel at both simultaneously.

Within the halls of the oldest arcane academies, students reaching this stage were once required to undertake endurance trials designed to test the limits of their Mana Wells. Some would cast continuously for hours, while others maintained complex enchantments throughout entire days.

Stories tell of legendary Spellblades whose Mana Wells became so deep that they could sustain magical warfare across entire campaigns. Though Rank 3 falls far short of such legends, it is often the first glimpse of what might one day become possible.

The deeper the well becomes, the more responsibility it demands. Power without discipline is dangerous, and a vast reservoir can be just as destructive to its wielder as it is to their enemies.

> "A pond may sustain a traveler. A lake may sustain a kingdom."
>
> — Archblade Seraph Valorian, Keeper of the Third Wellv

## Rank 4
### Description

Few Spellblades ever reach this stage.

The Mana Well has expanded into a vast reservoir capable of holding immense quantities of arcane energy. What once required careful conservation can now be sustained through entire battles, campaigns, and prolonged magical engagements.

At Rank 4, the Spellblade's connection to mana becomes second nature. The constant awareness of dwindling reserves fades into the background, replaced by confidence in the strength of their foundation. They possess enough energy to support advanced combat techniques while still maintaining reserves for unexpected threats.

The cultivation required to reach this level is immense. The body, mind, and soul must all be strengthened to withstand the pressure of such a large concentration of mana. Without discipline and training, the strain alone would be enough to cripple lesser practitioners.

Among the Spellblade Orders, Rank 4 is often viewed as the mark of a veteran. It is proof that the practitioner has survived years of training, battle, and refinement, building a Mana Well capable of supporting truly exceptional feats.

### Effects

- Increase your **Maximum Mana by ×12**.
- This multiplier is applied to your **Base Maximum Mana**.
- The additional mana becomes immediately available upon learning the talent.

#### Formula

Maximum Mana = Base Mana × 12

### Lore

The oldest records of the Arcane Blades speak of practitioners whose Mana Wells became so deep that they were compared to inland seas. Their reserves seemed inexhaustible to those around them, allowing them to maintain powerful techniques for astonishing lengths of time.

Within many Spellblade traditions, Rank 4 is regarded as a symbol of mastery over one's foundation. While greater power still lies ahead, few can deny the significance of reaching a stage where one's reserves dwarf those of ordinary spellcasters.

Veterans often warn younger Spellblades that a vast Mana Well is both a blessing and a burden. The temptation to rely solely upon overwhelming reserves can lead to arrogance, wastefulness, and eventual defeat.

The wisest masters understand that the purpose of a deep well is not to spend more recklessly, but to create more possibilities. The greater the reserve, the more choices remain available when others have none.

> "The difference between a novice and a master is not how much power they possess. It is how much remains when the battle is not yet over."
>
> — High Spellblade Arkanis Thorne, Warden of the Azure Depthsv

## Rank 5
### Description

The Mana Well has reached its pinnacle.

What began as a modest reservoir of arcane energy has become a vast ocean contained within the Spellblade's soul. The amount of mana available at this stage far exceeds what most practitioners will ever possess, allowing the Spellblade to sustain techniques, enchantments, and magical combat styles that would be impossible for lesser combatants.

At Rank 5, the Spellblade no longer worries about whether they possess enough mana to continue fighting. Instead, they concern themselves with how best to wield the immense reserves at their disposal. The challenge is no longer endurance, but mastery.

The cultivation required to reach this level is legendary. Every pathway within the body has been strengthened, every aspect of the soul tempered through years of training, combat, and arcane refinement. Few ever achieve such depth within their Mana Well, and those who do are often regarded as living legends among their peers.

This rank represents the culmination of the Spellblade's foundation. Every spell cast, every enchanted strike, and every future talent built upon arcane power draws strength from the immense reservoir created through Mana Well.

### Effects

- Increase your **Maximum Mana by ×15**.
- This multiplier is applied to your **Base Maximum Mana**.
- The additional mana becomes immediately available upon learning the talent.

#### Formula

Maximum Mana = Base Mana × 15

### Lore

Among the oldest Spellblade Orders, Rank 5 is often called **The Endless Reservoir**. It is said that a practitioner who reaches this stage possesses enough arcane endurance to fight battles that would exhaust entire companies of lesser spellcasters.

Ancient chronicles tell of legendary Spellblades who marched for days without rest, sustaining magical wards, empowering their weapons, and continuing to cast even as entire armies exhausted their reserves. Whether these stories are entirely true or embellished through centuries of retelling remains a matter of debate.

What is certain is that those who reach Rank 5 stand among the elite of their discipline. Their Mana Wells are so deep that they cease to be measured against ordinary standards. Their reserves become a defining aspect of their identity, spoken of with the same reverence as a master swordsman's skill or an archmage's knowledge.

Yet the wisest among them know a simple truth: even an ocean can be emptied if enough is taken from it. A vast Mana Well is not permission for recklessness, but the reward for discipline. Those who remember this lesson become legends. Those who forget it become cautionary tales.

> "The purpose of a great reservoir is not to spend without thought. It is to ensure that when the final moment arrives, you still have power left to give."
>
> — Grandmaster Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Prerequisites
None

## Scaling
See individual rank details.

## Synergy
Information coming soon.

## GM Notes
GM-only information coming soon.

entries.title: Arcane Guard
entries.body:
# Arcane Guard

## Overview
Spellblades understand that not every threat can be avoided through speed alone. Against hostile magic, they learn to shape mana into a protective barrier that surrounds their body, disrupting incoming spells before they can fully take hold.

Unlike Arcane Reflex, which relies upon agility and precise movement, Arcane Guard stands firm against magical assault. The Spellblade condenses raw mana into a shimmering defensive aura that absorbs and weakens hostile arcane energies, allowing them to endure attacks that would overwhelm lesser warriors.

At Rank I, the barrier is temporary and can only withstand modest magical punishment. Even so, it provides invaluable protection against enemy spellcasters, allowing the Spellblade to remain in the fight while closing the distance to their greatest threat.

## Rank 1
### Description

Spellblades understand that not every threat can be avoided through speed alone. Against hostile magic, they learn to shape mana into a protective barrier that surrounds their body, disrupting incoming spells before they can fully take hold.

Unlike Arcane Reflex, which relies upon agility and precise movement, Arcane Guard stands firm against magical assault. The Spellblade condenses raw mana into a shimmering defensive aura that absorbs and weakens hostile arcane energies, allowing them to endure attacks that would overwhelm lesser warriors.

At Rank I, the barrier is temporary and can only withstand modest magical punishment. Even so, it provides invaluable protection against enemy spellcasters, allowing the Spellblade to remain in the fight while closing the distance to their greatest threat.

### Effects

- Spend **20 MP** to activate **Arcane Guard**.
- Arcane Guard remains active for **3 Turns**.
- While active, gain **+2 on all Saving Throws against spells and magical abilities.**
- Reduce all magical damage you receive by **1d4**.
- Arcane Guard only protects the Spellblade.
- Arcane Guard cannot be activated again while already active.
- This talent does not reduce damage from non-magical attacks.

### Lore

Arcane Guard was developed after early Spellblades discovered that their greatest weakness was enemy spellcasters. While heavily armoured warriors could withstand blades and arrows, concentrated magical attacks often proved devastating before a Spellblade could close the distance.

Rather than abandoning their offensive style, the founders created a technique that allowed mana to defend as effectively as it could destroy. By weaving a protective current around their bodies, they learned to endure magical assaults long enough to bring the battle back into melee range.

Today, Arcane Guard is considered an essential technique within every Spellblade Order. Apprentices are taught that a master Spellblade should fear neither steel nor sorcery, for both can be answered with disciplined control over mana.

> *"Steel may break against armour, but magic breaks against a disciplined mind."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 2
### Description

As a Spellblade's understanding of defensive magic deepens, Arcane Guard evolves from a simple protective barrier into a resilient mantle of arcane energy. The flow of mana surrounding the Spellblade becomes steadier and more efficient, allowing it to intercept a greater amount of hostile magic without disrupting the warrior's rhythm in combat.

The barrier pulses in harmony with the Spellblade's mana core, weakening incoming spells before they fully manifest. Fire burns colder, lightning loses its bite, and curses struggle to take hold as the guard disperses part of the magical force before it reaches its target.

Rank II marks the beginning of true magical resilience. Veteran Spellblades rely on Arcane Guard to push through barrages of hostile magic, trusting their barrier to carry them safely into melee where their enemies are at their weakest.

### Effects

- Spend **25 MP** to activate **Arcane Guard**.
- Arcane Guard remains active for **4 Turns**.
- While active, gain **+3 on all Saving Throws against magical effects.**
- Reduce all magical damage you receive by **1d6**.
- Arcane Guard only protects the Spellblade.
- Arcane Guard cannot be activated again while already active.
- This rank replaces the effects of **Arcane Guard — Rank I**.

### Lore

Within the Spellblade Orders, Rank II is often called the **Warden's Mantle**. At this stage, apprentices stop fearing enemy spellcasters and begin treating hostile magic as another obstacle to overcome rather than an impossible threat.

Masters teach that Arcane Guard should never be relied upon to make a Spellblade invincible. Instead, it exists to buy precious moments—enough time to survive a devastating spell, close the distance, and bring the battle back to the edge of a blade.

Many famous Spellblades earned their reputations not by avoiding powerful magic, but by walking calmly through it. Their unwavering confidence inspired allies and unsettled enemy mages who watched their greatest spells lose much of their power against the shimmering barrier.

> *"Magic is only frightening until you learn to stand within the storm."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 3
### Description

Arcane Guard has become an instinctive defense, allowing the Spellblade to withstand powerful magical assaults without breaking their offensive momentum. The protective aura surrounding their body strengthens into a dense layer of mana that instinctively intercepts hostile magical energy before it reaches its target.

Rather than simply absorbing spells, the barrier disrupts and weakens the arcane structure holding them together. Flames lose their intensity, bolts of lightning fracture upon impact, and curses struggle to bind themselves to the Spellblade's soul. Although the barrier cannot completely negate powerful magic, it significantly reduces its effectiveness.

Rank III represents a turning point in a Spellblade's training. Having mastered both martial combat and magical resilience, they are capable of advancing directly into enemy spellcasters, trusting Arcane Guard to shield them while they close the distance.

### Effects

- Spend **30 MP** to activate **Arcane Guard**.
- Arcane Guard remains active for **5 Turns**.
- While active, gain **+4 on all Saving Throws against magical effects.**
- Reduce all magical damage you receive by **1d8**.
- Arcane Guard only protects the Spellblade.
- Arcane Guard cannot be activated again while already active.
- This rank replaces the effects of **Arcane Guard — Rank II**.

### Lore

Spellblade Masters refer to Rank III as the **Arcane Bastion**, a milestone where the barrier begins to function as naturally as breathing. The Spellblade no longer consciously maintains the ward; instead, their mana instinctively responds whenever hostile magic threatens them.

Throughout Asteria's history, many legendary Spellblades have survived encounters with powerful archmages through Arcane Guard alone. Rather than attempting to overpower devastating spells, they relied upon discipline, patience, and unwavering control of their own mana until they stood within striking distance.

Among the Orders, reaching Rank III is considered proof that a Spellblade has learned one of their greatest lessons: magic is not only a weapon to command, but a force that can be resisted through mastery and resolve.

> *"The strongest shield is not forged from steel, but from the unwavering will to endure."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 4
### Description

Arcane Guard has become a masterpiece of defensive spellcraft, allowing the Spellblade to stand firm against even the most destructive magical assaults. The protective barrier no longer simply absorbs hostile mana—it actively disrupts and disperses incoming magical energy before it can fully manifest.

When activated, shimmering currents of arcane energy envelop the Spellblade, constantly shifting to intercept hostile spells. Every wave of magical force that collides with the barrier is weakened as the guard redirects unstable mana harmlessly into the surrounding air. Veteran Spellblades often walk directly through magical bombardments, trusting their Arcane Guard to protect them while they close the distance to their prey.

Rank IV is regarded as the hallmark of an elite Spellblade. Those who achieve this level are feared by enemy mages, for they can withstand magical punishment that would overwhelm most warriors and continue advancing without hesitation.

### Effects

- Spend **35 MP** to activate **Arcane Guard**.
- Arcane Guard remains active for **6 Turns**.
- While active, gain **+5 on all Saving Throws against magical effects**.
- Reduce all magical damage you receive by **1d10**.
- Arcane Guard only protects the Spellblade.
- Arcane Guard cannot be activated again while already active.
- This rank replaces the effects of **Arcane Guard — Rank III**.

### Lore

Within the great Spellblade Orders, Rank IV is known as the **Magebreaker Ward**. It represents the point where enemy spellcasters begin to view the Spellblade not as a warrior to defeat, but as an unstoppable force that refuses to yield before arcane power.

Ancient battle records describe elite Spellblades advancing through storms of fire, lightning, and shadow while their shimmering wards steadily unravelled each spell before it could inflict its full devastation. Their resilience became legendary, inspiring allies while sowing doubt among even the most accomplished mages.

Masters teach that Arcane Guard is not about becoming immune to magic. It is about possessing the courage and discipline to continue advancing when every instinct tells others to retreat.

> *"The greatest victory over magic is not to destroy it, but to walk through it without fear."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 5
### Description

Arcane Guard reaches its ultimate form, surrounding the Spellblade in an almost impenetrable mantle of arcane energy. The barrier no longer merely resists hostile magic—it instinctively unravels and disperses magical attacks before they can reach their full potential. To enemy spellcasters, striking a master Spellblade feels like casting into a storm that tears their spells apart.

The barrier pulses in perfect harmony with the Spellblade's mana core, reinforcing itself with every passing moment. Even the most devastating magical assaults lose much of their strength as the guard absorbs, redirects, and dissipates hostile arcane energy. While no defence is absolute, Arcane Guard allows the Spellblade to endure magical punishment that few mortals could survive.

Only the greatest Spellblades achieve this level of mastery. They are renowned as Magebreakers, warriors who charge fearlessly into the heart of magical battlefields, trusting their discipline and mana to shield them from destruction.

### Effects

- Spend **40 MP** to activate **Arcane Guard**.
- Arcane Guard remains active for **8 Turns**.
- While active, gain **+6 on all Saving Throws against magical effects**.
- Reduce all magical damage you receive by **1d12**.
- The first magical effect each round that would inflict a negative status effect on you is made with **Disadvantage** (or the caster suffers a penalty, depending on the effect's rules).
- Arcane Guard only protects the Spellblade.
- Arcane Guard cannot be activated again while already active.
- This rank replaces the effects of **Arcane Guard — Rank IV**.

### Lore

Within the oldest Spellblade Orders, Rank V is known as the **Aegis of the Arcane**, a title reserved for masters whose command of defensive mana borders on legendary. They have learned that true protection is not created through overwhelming power, but through absolute control over the flow of magic itself.

Stories tell of Spellblades who walked unharmed through storms of fire, shattered curses with sheer force of will, and stood against archmages without yielding a single step. Whether these tales have grown through centuries of retelling is unknown, but they remain the ideal every apprentice strives to achieve.

To become a master of Arcane Guard is to embody one of the Spellblade's greatest philosophies: magic is neither feared nor worshipped—it is understood, mastered, and ultimately turned aside by unwavering discipline.

> *"The greatest shield is not forged from steel or stone. It is forged from a will that refuses to yield before magic."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Prerequisites
None

## Scaling
See individual rank details.

## Synergy
Information coming soon.

## GM Notes
GM-only information coming soon.

entries.title: Arcane Pursuit
entries.body:
# Arcane Pursuit

## Overview
Spellblades are taught that fleeing enemies create openings. Arcane Pursuit was developed to punish opponents who attempt to retreat, reposition, or escape the reach of a blade.

By locking onto the motion of a moving target, the Spellblade floods their body with mana and surges after them with explosive speed. Unlike Arcane Rush, which allows free repositioning, Arcane Pursuit is focused entirely on chasing movement. It does not carry the Spellblade wherever they wish to go; it carries them toward a target that has already begun to move.

At Rank I, Arcane Pursuit allows the Spellblade to close distance against enemies who attempt to flee or reposition. It is a reactive hunting technique, rewarding awareness and timing rather than simple speed.

## Rank 1
### Description

Spellblades are taught that fleeing enemies create openings. Arcane Pursuit was developed to punish opponents who attempt to retreat, reposition, or escape the reach of a blade.

By locking onto the motion of a moving target, the Spellblade floods their body with mana and surges after them with explosive speed. Unlike Arcane Rush, which allows free repositioning, Arcane Pursuit is focused entirely on chasing movement. It does not carry the Spellblade wherever they wish to go; it carries them toward a target that has already begun to move.

At Rank I, Arcane Pursuit allows the Spellblade to close distance against enemies who attempt to flee or reposition. It is a reactive hunting technique, rewarding awareness and timing rather than simple speed.

### Effects

- Spend **20 MP** to activate **Arcane Pursuit**.
- Choose one hostile creature within **10 metres** that has moved this turn.
- Instantly move to the nearest valid unoccupied space adjacent to that creature.
- This movement ignores difficult terrain.
- This movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks.
- After arriving, you may make **one melee weapon attack** against the chosen target.
- If no valid adjacent space exists, Arcane Pursuit fails.
- If Arcane Pursuit fails, you still spend **10 MP**.
- Arcane Pursuit cannot target creatures that have not moved this turn.

### Lore

Arcane Pursuit was created by Spellblades who refused to let enemies control the distance of battle. Archers, mages, and skirmishers often relied on movement to stay beyond the reach of melee warriors, but Spellblades answered with a technique designed to hunt motion itself.

The earliest masters described Arcane Pursuit as listening to the disturbance left behind by movement. Once a target shifted position, the Spellblade could follow that motion through mana, crossing the distance before the enemy fully escaped.

Among the Orders, apprentices are taught that Arcane Pursuit is not a charge. It is a response. The enemy moves first, and the Spellblade answers.

> *"Run if you wish. Every step only tells me where to follow."*
>
> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 2
### Description

As a Spellblade's mastery grows, Arcane Pursuit becomes faster, more precise, and capable of following enemies over greater distances. Rather than simply reacting to movement, the Spellblade begins to anticipate it, reading the flow of mana left in an opponent's wake before they have fully completed their reposition.

The burst of speed is almost instantaneous. To spectators, the Spellblade appears to vanish in a flash of arcane light before materialising beside their quarry, denying even the most agile foes the opportunity to escape.

At Rank II, Arcane Pursuit extends its reach and improves its efficiency, allowing the Spellblade to relentlessly pressure enemies who rely on movement to survive. Those who believe a few extra metres will save them quickly discover that distance means little to a determined Spellblade.

### Effects

- Spend **25 MP** to activate **Arcane Pursuit**.
- Choose one hostile creature within **15 metres** that has moved this turn.
- Instantly move to the nearest valid unoccupied space adjacent to that creature.
- This movement ignores difficult terrain.
- This movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks.
- After arriving, you may make **one melee weapon attack** against the chosen target.
- If no valid adjacent space exists, Arcane Pursuit fails.
- If Arcane Pursuit fails, you still spend **12 MP** (rounded down).
- Arcane Pursuit cannot target creatures that have not moved this turn.
- This rank replaces the effects of **Arcane Pursuit — Rank I**.

### Lore

Within the Spellblade Orders, Rank II is known as the **Hunter's Step**. Apprentices begin to realise that Arcane Pursuit is not powered by speed alone, but by recognising the arcane disturbance created when a creature moves across the battlefield.

Veteran Spellblades often describe the sensation as chasing an echo rather than a body. Every movement leaves behind a fleeting trail of mana that an experienced practitioner can instinctively follow, allowing them to intercept enemies before they can capitalise on their new position.

Many skirmishers and battle mages have learned to fear this technique. The moment they choose to retreat, they also choose to invite the Spellblade into striking distance.

> *"Every step your enemy takes leaves a trail. Learn to follow it, and no one truly escapes."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 3
### Description

Arcane Pursuit has evolved into one of the Spellblade's most feared battlefield techniques. By reading the flow of mana left behind by moving creatures, the Spellblade can instantly close even greater distances, denying opponents the opportunity to disengage safely.

The pursuit is no longer simply a burst of speed. It becomes an act of prediction, allowing the Spellblade to intercept fleeing enemies before they can establish a new position. To an observer, the Spellblade appears to disappear into a streak of arcane light, emerging beside their target with flawless precision.

At Rank III, Arcane Pursuit allows experienced Spellblades to relentlessly pressure mobile opponents, forcing enemies to think twice before attempting to reposition during combat.

### Effects

- Spend **30 MP** to activate **Arcane Pursuit**.
- Choose one hostile creature within **20 metres** that has moved this turn.
- Instantly move to the nearest valid unoccupied space adjacent to that creature.
- This movement ignores difficult terrain and does not provoke Opportunity Attacks.
- Immediately after arriving, you may make **one melee weapon attack** against the chosen target.
- If no valid adjacent space exists, Arcane Pursuit fails.
- If Arcane Pursuit fails, you still spend **15 MP**.
- Arcane Pursuit cannot target creatures that have not moved this turn.
- This rank replaces the effects of **Arcane Pursuit — Rank II**.

### Lore

Spellblade masters refer to Rank III as the **Relentless Pursuit**, the stage where distance begins to lose its meaning. Practitioners no longer chase an enemy's footsteps; they instinctively follow the lingering currents of mana disturbed by movement itself.

Throughout Asteria's history, countless generals have underestimated this technique, believing a tactical withdrawal would create breathing room against a Spellblade. Instead, they found the arcane warrior already standing beside them before their formation could recover.

Among the Orders, students are reminded that Arcane Pursuit is not about moving faster than an opponent. It is about ensuring that movement itself becomes a liability.

> *"The moment your enemy chooses to flee is the moment they have already been caught."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 4
### Description

The Spellblade has refined Arcane Pursuit into a technique that borders on supernatural. Rather than merely chasing a moving opponent, they instinctively predict where their quarry will be, allowing them to intercept even the swiftest combatants before they can gain an advantage.

At this level, Arcane Pursuit becomes a terrifying display of battlefield dominance. Every attempted retreat, tactical reposition, or desperate escape risks placing the Spellblade directly beside their target. Those who rely upon mobility quickly discover that every movement creates another opportunity for pursuit.

Veteran Spellblades often describe Rank IV as the point where the hunter no longer follows their prey—they simply arrive where the prey intends to be.

### Effects

- Spend **35 MP** to activate **Arcane Pursuit**.
- Choose one hostile creature within **25 metres** that has moved this turn.
- Instantly move to the nearest valid unoccupied space adjacent to that creature.
- This movement ignores difficult terrain and does not provoke Opportunity Attacks.
- Immediately after arriving, you may make **one melee weapon attack** against the chosen target.
- If the attack hits, the target's **Movement Speed is reduced by 50% until the end of its next turn.**
- If no valid adjacent space exists, Arcane Pursuit fails.
- If Arcane Pursuit fails, you still spend **17 MP** (half the Mana Cost, rounded down).
- Arcane Pursuit cannot target creatures that have not moved this turn.
- This rank replaces the effects of **Arcane Pursuit — Rank III**.

### Lore

Rank IV is known within the Spellblade Orders as the **Hunter's Mark**, not because it brands an enemy with magic, but because few creatures escape once a master Spellblade has chosen to pursue them.

Military records speak of elite Spellblades who specialised in hunting enemy commanders, scouts, and battle mages. Attempts to retreat often proved futile, as the Spellblade would appear beside their target before orders could even be given.

Masters teach that Arcane Pursuit is more than a technique—it is a promise. Once a Spellblade commits to the chase, the battle is no longer fought on the enemy's terms.

> *"Movement creates opportunity. For my enemy, it is the opportunity to be caught."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 5
### Description

Arcane Pursuit reaches its ultimate form, allowing the Spellblade to hunt even the fastest opponents across the battlefield. Through complete mastery of mana and movement, they no longer react to where an enemy has been—they instinctively intercept where they are attempting to go.

To witnesses, the technique appears impossible. A fleeing opponent takes only a few steps before the Spellblade vanishes in a surge of arcane energy, materialising beside them with blade already in motion. Distance offers no safety, and movement itself becomes a dangerous gamble.

Only the greatest Spellblades ever master Arcane Pursuit to this degree. Those who do become relentless hunters, capable of punishing any enemy who believes they can escape the reach of steel and sorcery.

### Effects

- Spend **40 MP** to activate **Arcane Pursuit**.
- Choose one hostile creature within **30 metres** that has moved this turn.
- Instantly move to the nearest valid unoccupied space adjacent to that creature.
- This movement ignores difficult terrain and does not provoke Opportunity Attacks.
- Immediately after arriving, you may make **one melee weapon attack** against the chosen target.
- If the attack hits, the target's **Movement Speed becomes 0 until the end of its next turn**.
- If no valid adjacent space exists, Arcane Pursuit fails.
- If Arcane Pursuit fails, you still spend **20 MP**.
- Arcane Pursuit cannot target creatures that have not moved this turn.
- This rank replaces the effects of **Arcane Pursuit — Rank IV**.

### Lore

Within the oldest Spellblade Orders, Rank V is known as the **Unbroken Chase**. It represents the pinnacle of pursuit magic, where distance, obstacles, and momentum cease to matter. The Spellblade no longer follows an enemy—they simply deny them the ability to escape.

Stories of the Unbroken Chase are common throughout Asteria. Assassins who vanished into crowded streets, battle mages who blinked across fortifications, and monsters that outran entire companies have all fallen to Spellblades who mastered this technique. Their prey quickly learned that every attempt to flee only hastened the inevitable.

To a master of Arcane Pursuit, movement is not an obstacle to overcome—it is an invitation to strike.

> *"You may outrun a soldier. You may outpace a knight. But once a Spellblade begins the chase, your journey ends where my blade begins."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Prerequisites
None

GM-only information coming soon.

entries.title: Arcane Tempo
entries.body:
# Arcane Tempo

## Overview
A Spellblade's greatest strength is not their sword or their magic, but the rhythm between the two. Arcane Tempo teaches the practitioner to seamlessly flow from spellcasting into swordplay, then back again, creating an ever-changing dance of steel and mana that keeps opponents constantly off balance.

Upon activating Arcane Tempo, mana courses through the Spellblade's body, synchronising every movement with their spellcasting. Each successful spell naturally leads into a more precise weapon strike, while every successful strike prepares the mind and body to cast with greater focus. The technique rewards versatility rather than repetition, encouraging the Spellblade to weave martial combat and magic together as a single discipline.

At Rank I, the rhythm is still fragile and easily broken, but even novice Spellblades quickly discover that maintaining their Tempo allows them to fight with greater efficiency than relying on blade or spell alone.

## Rank 1
### Description

A Spellblade's greatest strength is not their sword or their magic, but the rhythm between the two. Arcane Tempo teaches the practitioner to seamlessly flow from spellcasting into swordplay, then back again, creating an ever-changing dance of steel and mana that keeps opponents constantly off balance.

Upon activating Arcane Tempo, mana courses through the Spellblade's body, synchronising every movement with their spellcasting. Each successful spell naturally leads into a more precise weapon strike, while every successful strike prepares the mind and body to cast with greater focus. The technique rewards versatility rather than repetition, encouraging the Spellblade to weave martial combat and magic together as a single discipline.

At Rank I, the rhythm is still fragile and easily broken, but even novice Spellblades quickly discover that maintaining their Tempo allows them to fight with greater efficiency than relying on blade or spell alone.

### Effects

- Spend **20 MP** to activate **Arcane Tempo**.
- Arcane Tempo remains active for **5 Turns**.
- After successfully casting a spell, your **next melee weapon attack** gains **+1 to its Attack Roll**.
- After successfully hitting with a melee weapon attack, your **next spell** gains **+1 to its Spell Attack Roll** or **Spell Save DC** (whichever is applicable).
- Each bonus is consumed after it is applied.
- Arcane Tempo only functions while alternating between spellcasting and melee weapon attacks.
- Repeating the same action (casting a spell after a spell, or attacking after an attack) does not generate a new bonus.

### Lore

Among the Spellblade Orders, Arcane Tempo is often called the **Rhythm of Battle**. Masters teach that a true Spellblade should never become predictable. Every spell should naturally flow into a strike, and every strike should prepare the next spell, creating a combat style that is fluid, relentless, and impossible to anticipate.

Many apprentices struggle with this lesson, instinctively favouring either magic or swordsmanship. Only through discipline do they learn that the greatest strength lies not in choosing one path, but in mastering the rhythm that unites them.

> *"Do not think of casting, then striking. Think only of the rhythm, and both will become one."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 2
### Description

The Spellblade's understanding of Arcane Tempo deepens, allowing the rhythm between sword and spell to become far more natural. No longer forcing the transition between martial and magical techniques, the Spellblade begins to move instinctively, allowing each action to flow seamlessly into the next.

Mana circulates continuously throughout the Spellblade's body, synchronising every strike and every spell into a single combat rhythm. As this tempo builds, attacks become more accurate and spells are woven with greater precision, making it increasingly difficult for opponents to predict what will come next.

At Rank II, maintaining the rhythm becomes easier and more rewarding. Experienced Spellblades understand that every successful transition strengthens the flow of battle, while hesitation or repetition causes the tempo to falter. Those who master this balance become exceptionally adaptable, shifting effortlessly between blade and sorcery as the battle unfolds.

### Effects

- Spend **25 MP** to activate **Arcane Tempo**.
- Arcane Tempo remains active for **6 Turns**.
- After successfully casting a spell, your **next melee weapon attack** gains **+2 to its Attack Roll**.
- After successfully hitting with a melee weapon attack, your **next spell** gains **+2 to its Spell Attack Roll** or **Spell Save DC** (whichever is applicable).
- Each bonus is consumed after it is applied.
- Arcane Tempo only functions while alternating between spellcasting and melee weapon attacks.
- Repeating the same action (casting a spell after a spell, or attacking after an attack) does not generate a new bonus.
- This rank replaces the effects of **Arcane Tempo — Rank I**.

### Lore

Within the Spellblade Orders, Rank II is known as the **Flowing Rhythm**, where combat begins to resemble a carefully choreographed dance rather than a series of separate actions. Masters teach that the blade should prepare the spell, and the spell should prepare the blade, creating a cycle that never truly ends.

Many apprentices discover that maintaining Arcane Tempo requires discipline rather than speed. A reckless warrior quickly loses their rhythm, while a patient Spellblade allows every action to naturally lead into the next. This philosophy becomes the foundation upon which all advanced Spellblade techniques are built.

> *"A true rhythm cannot be rushed. Every strike has a spell waiting behind it, and every spell already knows where the next strike will fall."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 3
### Description

The Spellblade has begun to master the rhythm between blade and spell, maintaining a continuous flow of martial and arcane techniques throughout combat. Every successful transition strengthens their momentum, allowing attacks to become more precise while spells are cast with unwavering confidence.

Mana pulses through the Spellblade in perfect harmony with each movement, linking every strike and spell into a single, uninterrupted sequence. Rather than viewing swordsmanship and spellcasting as separate disciplines, the Spellblade embraces them as two halves of the same combat style. Opponents quickly find themselves overwhelmed by the relentless change in tempo, unable to predict whether the next attack will be steel or sorcery.

Rank III represents the point where Arcane Tempo becomes instinctive. The Spellblade no longer needs to consciously maintain the rhythm—it simply becomes part of the way they fight.

### Effects

- Spend **30 MP** to activate **Arcane Tempo**.
- Arcane Tempo remains active for **7 Turns**.
- After successfully casting a spell, your **next melee weapon attack** gains **+3 to its Attack Roll**.
- After successfully hitting with a melee weapon attack, your **next spell** gains **+3 to its Spell Attack Roll** or **Spell Save DC** (whichever is applicable).
- Each bonus is consumed after it is applied.
- Arcane Tempo only functions while alternating between spellcasting and melee weapon attacks.
- Repeating the same action (casting a spell after a spell, or attacking after an attack) does not generate a new bonus.
- This rank replaces the effects of **Arcane Tempo — Rank II**.

### Lore

Among veteran Spellblades, Rank III is known as the **Battle Rhythm**. Reaching this stage signifies that the practitioner has stopped thinking about when to attack or when to cast. Instead, every action naturally leads into the next, creating a seamless dance of steel and mana.

Masters often describe watching an accomplished Spellblade as listening to a symphony. Every spell, every strike, and every movement flows together with perfect timing, leaving opponents unable to anticipate the next beat. It is this unpredictable rhythm that has earned the Spellblade their reputation as one of Asteria's most versatile warriors.

> *"The finest battles are never won through strength alone, but through perfect rhythm. When steel and sorcery share the same heartbeat, victory follows."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 4
### Description

The Spellblade's rhythm has become unwavering, allowing them to recover from mistakes without losing the flow of battle. Where lesser practitioners falter after a missed strike or disrupted spell, a master of Arcane Tempo adapts instantly, seamlessly continuing the dance between steel and sorcery.

Every movement is guided by instinct. Mana circulates effortlessly throughout the Spellblade's body, ensuring that every spell naturally transitions into a weapon strike and every successful strike prepares the next spell. Even when an attack fails to find its mark, the Spellblade's rhythm remains intact, denying their opponent the opportunity to disrupt their momentum.

Rank IV represents the mastery of consistency. The Spellblade no longer relies upon perfect execution to maintain their Tempo, making them an exceptionally difficult opponent to slow or interrupt.

### Effects

- Spend **35 MP** to activate **Arcane Tempo**.
- Arcane Tempo remains active for **8 Turns**.
- After successfully casting a spell, your **next melee weapon attack** gains **+4 to its Attack Roll**.
- After successfully hitting with a melee weapon attack, your **next spell** gains **+4 to its Spell Attack Roll** or **Spell Save DC** (whichever is applicable).
- Each bonus is consumed after it is applied.
- If your empowered melee attack misses, the bonus is retained until your next melee weapon attack.
- If your empowered spell fails to hit or the target succeeds on its saving throw, the bonus is retained until your next spell.
- Arcane Tempo only functions while alternating between spellcasting and melee weapon attacks.
- This rank replaces the effects of **Arcane Tempo — Rank III**.

### Lore

Spellblade Masters call this stage the **Endless Rhythm**, for the flow of battle can no longer be broken by simple mistakes. The practitioner has learned that true mastery is measured not by perfection, but by the ability to recover instantly and continue fighting without hesitation.

Veterans often compare Arcane Tempo to the beating of a heart. It does not stop because one step is misplaced or one strike goes astray. Instead, it continues without interruption, carrying the Spellblade forward until the battle is won.

To witness a master of Arcane Tempo is to see steel and sorcery move with absolute harmony, every action flowing effortlessly into the next without pause.

> *"Perfection is not never stumbling. Perfection is never losing the rhythm when you do."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 5
### Description

Arcane Tempo reaches its highest form, becoming more than a combat technique—it becomes the natural rhythm of the Spellblade's soul. Every spell seamlessly transitions into a strike, and every strike naturally prepares the next spell. The distinction between martial skill and spellcasting disappears entirely, replaced by a flawless cycle of steel and sorcery.

The Spellblade no longer fights by making individual decisions. Instead, they surrender to the flow of battle itself, allowing instinct and discipline to guide every movement. Opponents struggle to keep pace as the Spellblade effortlessly shifts between devastating spells and precise weapon strikes, maintaining relentless pressure without ever losing momentum.

Masters of Arcane Tempo are recognised throughout Asteria as living embodiments of the Spellblade philosophy. To face one is to battle a warrior whose every action strengthens the next, creating an unbroken chain of perfectly timed attacks and spells.

### Effects

- Spend **40 MP** to activate **Arcane Tempo**.
- Arcane Tempo remains active for **10 Turns**.
- After successfully casting a spell, your **next melee weapon attack** gains **+5 to its Attack Roll**.
- After successfully hitting with a melee weapon attack, your **next spell** gains **+5 to its Spell Attack Roll** or **Spell Save DC** (whichever is applicable).
- Each bonus is consumed after it is applied.
- If your empowered melee attack misses, the bonus is retained until your next melee weapon attack.
- If your empowered spell fails to hit or the target succeeds on its saving throw, the bonus is retained until your next spell.
- Each time you successfully alternate between casting a spell and landing a melee weapon attack, **extend Arcane Tempo's remaining duration by 1 Turn**, up to its original maximum duration.
- This rank replaces the effects of **Arcane Tempo — Rank IV**.

### Lore

Within the oldest Spellblade Orders, Rank V is known as the **Perfect Tempo**. It is said that those who achieve this level no longer think about whether to cast or strike, for both actions have become a single expression of their will.

Legend speaks of masters who fought for entire battles without ever breaking their rhythm, maintaining an endless cycle of blade and magic that left their opponents unable to predict or interrupt their relentless assault. Every successful transition renewed their momentum, allowing them to dictate the pace of the fight until victory was inevitable.

To master Arcane Tempo is to understand the heart of the Spellblade. Steel and sorcery are not separate disciplines, but two notes within the same song.

> *"Do not master the blade. Do not master the spell. Master the rhythm between them, and both will follow."*

> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Prerequisites
None

## Scaling
See individual rank details.

## Synergy
Information coming soon.

## GM Notes
GM-only information coming soon.

entries.body:
# Mana Infusion

## Overview
A Spellblade soon learns that victory is not determined by how much mana they possess, but by how efficiently they can recover it. Through Mana Infusion, the Spellblade floods their body with arcane energy, allowing every successful strike to draw lingering magical essence from the battlefield and recycle it back into themselves.

While Arcane Edge channels mana into a weapon, Mana Infusion channels mana into the Spellblade's body. Every swing becomes part of a continuous cycle—mana is spent to enhance their abilities, then partially recovered through the rhythm of combat. The harder the Spellblade presses the attack, the longer they can maintain their momentum.

At Rank I, the infusion is still unstable, allowing only a small amount of mana and stamina to be reclaimed. Even so, this technique marks the beginning of the Spellblade's mastery over sustained combat, rewarding those who remain aggressive without becoming reckless.

## Rank 1
### Description

A Spellblade soon learns that victory is not determined by how much mana they possess, but by how efficiently they can recover it. Through Mana Infusion, the Spellblade floods their body with arcane energy, allowing every successful strike to draw lingering magical essence from the battlefield and recycle it back into themselves.

While Arcane Edge channels mana into a weapon, Mana Infusion channels mana into the Spellblade's body. Every swing becomes part of a continuous cycle—mana is spent to enhance their abilities, then partially recovered through the rhythm of combat. The harder the Spellblade presses the attack, the longer they can maintain their momentum.

At Rank I, the infusion is still unstable, allowing only a small amount of mana and stamina to be reclaimed. Even so, this technique marks the beginning of the Spellblade's mastery over sustained combat, rewarding those who remain aggressive without becoming reckless.

### Effects

- Spend **12 MP & 5 SP** to activate **Mana Infusion**.
- Mana Infusion remains active for **4 Turns**.
- **Once per turn**, the first successful melee weapon attack restores:
  - **3 Mana (MP)**
  - **3 Stamina (SP)**
- The restored resources cannot exceed your maximum MP or SP.
- Requires a melee weapon to trigger the restoration effect.
- Mana Infusion cannot be activated again while already active.

### Lore

The earliest Spellblades believed that mana should never simply be expended. They observed that every clash of enchanted steel disturbed the natural flow of arcane energy, releasing fragments of magical essence into the surrounding world. Through years of experimentation, they discovered how to reclaim a portion of that energy before it dissipated.

This technique became known as Mana Infusion, not because it grants unlimited power, but because it teaches the Spellblade to fight in harmony with the flow of mana itself. Every successful strike becomes an opportunity to recover, allowing experienced Spellblades to remain in battle long after others have exhausted their strength.

Among the veteran Orders, apprentices are taught that Mana Infusion is a lesson in balance. A Spellblade who spends wisely and recovers efficiently will often outlast an opponent who relies only on overwhelming force.

> *"The greatest warriors are not those who spend the most power, but those who know how to reclaim it."*
>
> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 2
### Description

The Spellblade's mastery of Mana Infusion grows as they learn to draw greater amounts of energy from every successful strike. Rather than merely recovering fragments of their own expended mana, they instinctively absorb the lingering arcane energy released through combat, allowing them to sustain both their magical and physical endurance for longer engagements.

With improved control, the infusion becomes more stable and efficient. Mana flows continuously through the Spellblade's body, reinforcing muscles, calming fatigue, and restoring the magical reserves required to fuel their combat techniques. Every successful blow strengthens the cycle, rewarding those who maintain constant pressure against their opponents.

Rank II teaches the Spellblade that victory is not won through overwhelming force alone, but through endurance. A disciplined Spellblade who manages their resources carefully can continue fighting long after others have exhausted themselves.

### Effects

- Spend **12 MP & 5 SP**  to activate **Mana Infusion**.
- Mana Infusion remains active for **5 Turns**.
- **Once per turn**, the first successful melee weapon attack restores:
  - **5 Mana (MP)**
  - **5 Stamina (SP)**
- The restored resources cannot exceed your maximum MP or SP.
- Requires a melee weapon to trigger the restoration effect.
- Mana Infusion cannot be activated again while already active.

### Lore

Among experienced Spellblades, Rank II is often known as the **Flowing Cycle**. At this stage, the practitioner no longer sees mana as a resource that is simply spent and lost. Instead, they begin to understand that battle itself is filled with arcane energy waiting to be reclaimed.

Masters teach that every clash of enchanted steel leaves traces of magical essence within the battlefield. While most warriors allow this energy to fade into the world, Spellblades learn to instinctively draw it back into themselves, creating a continuous cycle of expenditure and recovery.

Many veteran Spellblades attribute their endurance not to larger mana reserves, but to their ability to replenish those reserves while remaining in the heart of battle. It is this relentless efficiency that separates a seasoned Spellblade from an ordinary warrior.

> *"Mana is never truly lost. The wise simply know where to find it again."*
>
> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Wellv

## Rank 3
### Description

The Spellblade's mastery over Mana Infusion has become second nature, allowing them to sustain themselves through the flow of battle with remarkable efficiency. Every successful strike strengthens the connection between their body and the surrounding arcane currents, drawing greater amounts of energy back into their reserves.

Rather than simply recovering spent mana, the Spellblade establishes a continuous cycle of expenditure and restoration. Mana fuels their techniques, their techniques empower their strikes, and those strikes replenish the very energy that was spent. This harmonious cycle allows experienced Spellblades to remain effective even during prolonged engagements where other warriors begin to tire.

At Rank III, Mana Infusion becomes a defining combat technique of the Spellblade. The ability rewards relentless pressure and careful resource management, allowing the Spellblade to maintain both their magical and physical endurance while remaining at the forefront of battle.

### Effects

- Spend **12 MP & 5 SP** to activate **Mana Infusion**.
- Mana Infusion remains active for **6 Turns**.
- **Once per turn**, the first successful melee weapon attack restores:
  - **7 Mana (MP)**
  - **7 Stamina (SP)**
- The restored resources cannot exceed your maximum MP or SP.
- Requires a melee weapon to trigger the restoration effect.
- Mana Infusion cannot be activated again while already active.

### Lore

Spellblade veterans often refer to Rank III as the **Living Current**, the stage where mana begins to flow naturally through every action rather than being consciously directed. The Spellblade no longer fights against exhaustion—they fight alongside the rhythm of mana itself.

Historical records describe legendary warriors who maintained their magical strength throughout battles lasting hours, not because they possessed limitless reserves, but because every successful strike replenished a portion of what had been spent. Their enemies watched in disbelief as the Spellblade continued to cast spells and empower their weapon long after others would have been exhausted.

Within the Spellblade Orders, reaching Rank III is considered proof that a warrior has learned one of the discipline's greatest lessons: true strength comes not from possessing endless power, but from ensuring that power never stops flowing.

> *"The strongest current is not the one that burns brightest, but the one that never ceases to flow."*
>
> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 4
### Description

The Spellblade has mastered the flow of Mana Infusion to the point where every successful strike draws substantial energy back into both body and soul. The infusion becomes remarkably efficient, allowing the Spellblade to maintain an aggressive fighting style without quickly exhausting their magical or physical reserves.

Mana flows continuously throughout the Spellblade's body, reinforcing every movement and creating a powerful cycle of expenditure and recovery. As spells are cast and techniques are unleashed, successful attacks replenish the energy needed to continue fighting, allowing the Spellblade to maintain relentless pressure throughout extended encounters.

At Rank IV, Mana Infusion becomes one of the defining techniques of veteran Spellblades. Masters of the art understand that victory is often earned through endurance as much as raw power, and those who can continuously recover their strength become exceptionally difficult to outlast.

### Effects

- Spend **35 MP** to activate **Mana Infusion**.
- Mana Infusion remains active for **7 Turns**.
- **Once per turn**, the first successful melee weapon attack restores:
  - **10 Mana (MP)**
  - **10 Stamina (SP)**
- The restored resources cannot exceed your maximum MP or SP.
- Requires a melee weapon to trigger the restoration effect.
- Mana Infusion cannot be activated again while already active.
- This rank replaces the effects of **Mana Infusion — Rank III**.

### Lore

Among the Spellblade Orders, Rank IV is known as the **Endless Current**. Reaching this stage signifies that the Spellblade has developed an intuitive understanding of the relationship between combat and mana, allowing them to recover strength almost as quickly as it is spent.

Veteran instructors often teach that this technique is less about reclaiming power and more about refusing to waste it. Every successful strike becomes an opportunity to sustain the flow of battle, ensuring that no fragment of arcane energy is lost without purpose.

Many legendary Spellblades have survived battles against overwhelming odds through Mana Infusion alone. While others slowly succumbed to fatigue, they continued fighting with unwavering determination, drawing strength from every successful blow until victory was finally secured.

> *"Power fades. Endurance wins wars. Learn the difference, and your mana will never truly abandon you."*
>
> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Rank 5
### Description

Mana Infusion reaches its pinnacle as the Spellblade masters the endless cycle of expenditure and recovery. Rather than simply consuming mana to fuel their abilities, they have learned to weave themselves into the natural flow of arcane energy, reclaiming strength with every decisive strike. Their body becomes a living conduit where magical and physical energy exist in perfect harmony.

When Mana Infusion is activated, arcane currents surge through every muscle, vein, and nerve. Each successful blow draws lingering mana from the battlefield and channels it back into the Spellblade, while simultaneously revitalising their physical endurance. The rhythm of combat itself becomes a source of power, allowing them to sustain prolonged engagements that would leave even seasoned warriors exhausted.

Only the greatest Spellblades ever achieve this level of mastery. To them, battle is no longer a race to see who can spend the most power, but who can maintain their strength the longest. Their opponents often watch in frustration as the Spellblade continues to recover mana and stamina throughout the fight, refusing to slow until victory has been secured.

### Effects

- Spend **40 MP** to activate **Mana Infusion**.
- Mana Infusion remains active for **8 Turns**.
- **Once per turn**, the first successful melee weapon attack restores:
  - **15 Mana (MP)**
  - **15 Stamina (SP)**
- The restored resources cannot exceed your maximum MP or SP.
- Requires a melee weapon to trigger the restoration effect.
- Mana Infusion cannot be activated again while already active.
- This rank replaces the effects of **Mana Infusion — Rank IV**.

### Lore

Among the oldest Spellblade Orders, Rank V is known as the **Eternal Flow**, a title reserved for those who have achieved complete harmony between body, weapon, and mana. Masters no longer view mana as a finite resource to be carefully guarded. Instead, they understand that every clash of enchanted steel releases energy that can be reclaimed through discipline and flawless technique.

Legends speak of Spellblades who fought through entire campaigns without once exhausting their magical reserves. While others rested to recover, these masters simply continued forward, their strength renewed with every successful strike. Whether these stories have been exaggerated through centuries of retelling is unknown, but they remain an inspiration to every aspiring Spellblade.

To master Mana Infusion is to embrace one of the core philosophies of the Spellblade: power is not measured by how much mana you possess, but by how efficiently you can wield it. The greatest warriors are those who never allow the flow to stop.

> *"The river does not fear running dry, for it is always fed by its own current. Fight the same way."*  
> — Grand Spellblade Aetherion Lux, First Blade of the Infinite Well

## Prerequisites
None

## Scaling
See individual rank details.

## Synergy
Information coming soon.

## GM Notes
GM-only information coming soon.
